newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia parliament starts debate on new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia parliament starts debate on new cabinet.

text.p: The Slovenian parliament headed for a vote on Thursday on a new cabinet presented by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek two weeks ago following an inconclusive general election on November 10.
"I am sure this is a good line-up, a combination of knowledge, experience and freshness," Drnovsek told parliament at the beginning of a televised debate preceding the vote.
The new government will be the third since Slovenia gained independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991.

Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats last month formed a coalition with the ex-communist United List of Social Democrats, the pensioners' party Desus and the Nationalist Party. His government has a majority of just one vote.
Out of 18 ministerial candidates, six failed to gain approval from parliamentary bodies, but Drnovsek decided he would not replace any of them.
Among key posts, the nominees for finance minister, Mitja Gaspari, and interior minister, Polonca Dobrajc, did not get approval.

Three rightist parties in the "Spring" alliance, comprising the conservative People's Party, the centre-right Social Democrats and the Christian Democrats, said they would vote against Drnovsek's government line-up. The group holds 44 out of the 90 parliamentary seats.

"This government will not be capable of performing the key tasks, like a reform of the social security system, the pension system and joining the European Union," said Miroslav Mozetic, the Christian Democrats' chief whip.
If the alliance succeeds in voting down Drnovsek, the prime minister must present a new government list within 10 days.
